clue.text: Customs! They seized the mine, unfortunately

parts.note: mores are the customs and conventions of a society

indicators.note: the word They grips the next piece between its letters, as a captor would

parts.note: taken as written
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A lament that customs officers took over a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs!' with its exclamation looks like an officer's cry; it is the plural noun for social conventions. 'the' before 'mine' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiomatic expression of regret, the same as saying sadly or alas.

clue.text: Setter's backing currency with a girl of the 17

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters of the setter's phrase run the other way

parts.note: the setter's is 'I am', shortened to I'M
the rand is the South African currency

explanation.surface: The setter supports a currency alongside a girl from a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IM into MI. The 17 is the answer to 17-down, Shakespeare's The Tempest, in which Miranda is Prospero's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Miranda is the daughter of Prospero, the young heroine of Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Told of 1, 5 and 25

definitions.meaning: connected by family: Miranda is daughter to Prospero, and Antonio is his brother

explanation.definitionFit: Narrated is a synonym for told, and kin are linked by blood, so the word fits both senses.

clue.text: Bright star is ours, orbiting by means of eggs

indicators.note: going round, so the star surrounds the next piece

parts.note: the star that is ours is the sun
per is Latin for by means of, as in per post
ova are eggs

explanation.surface: A bright star belongs to us, circling thanks to eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ours' stands for the star that belongs to us; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is an exploding star that briefly shines with enormous brightness.

clue.text: From my dacha it is over 600 miles to Caracas

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone notes the distance from their country cottage to the Venezuelan capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A dacha is a Russian country house, which makes the surface sound like a trip abroad; the definition describes a place by its distance from Caracas in Venezuela.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean island nation lies a little over six hundred miles north of Venezuela's capital.

clue.text: 17 maker briefly to do well

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: the magician who conjures the storm in The Tempest (17-down) is Prospero

explanation.surface: Whoever made a storm briefly does well.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 refers to 17-down, The Tempest: Prospero raises the storm that opens the play. 'briefly' removes his final O.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish or succeed is to thrive, which is what doing well means.

clue.text: Conclusion of great success, but put up for old-fashioned wash

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: a win is a success

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Great success ends, but is set aside for a dated laundry day.
explanation.walkthrough: A twin-tub is a washing machine with separate wash and spin drums, common in Britain before automatic machines; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-tub is a dated type of washing machine, so it stands for an old-style laundering.

clue.text: Winter slogan: provide for dished and bereft

indicators.note: the letters supplied are rearranged to provide the answer

explanation.surface: A winter appeal urges help for those who are ruined and destitute.
explanation.walkthrough: DISHED and BEREFT together have exactly the letters needed; 'and' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting out food for garden birds is a familiar cold-weather appeal by wildlife charities.

clue.text: Cover for the "Listener" when Wyatt catches retreating boy

indicators.note: the lawman's surname holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was the famous Wild West lawman

indicators.note: going backwards, so the boy's name runs right to left

parts.note: Alf is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A Wild West marshal grabs a fleeing lad to cover a listener.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around Listener flag that it means an ear, not the magazine of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap on a hat that folds down protects the ear, the organ a listener uses.

clue.text: I don't exactly mean that Fe is tritium

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
taken as written
T is the chemical symbol for tritium

explanation.surface: A speaker hedges about whether iron really is tritium.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who uses irony says things they do not literally intend, which the clue's speaker confesses.

clue.text: Novel heroine left in bliss to the making of mosaics

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Hardy's novel heroine

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left is placed inside the word for bliss

parts.note: elation is great happiness

explanation.surface: A fictional heroine's leftover joy goes into mosaic work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside ELATION after its E, giving ELLATION; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiling a surface with fitted shapes, as in mosaic work, is called by this term.

clue.text: Old Hollywood actor had gold he gave to charity

parts.note: Robert Donat was a star of 1930s films such as Goodbye, Mr Chips
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A film star of yesteryear donated his gold to a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A giver of money or goods to a cause is a donor, and this is an older form of the word.

clue.text: Momentum first encountered by American without power

parts.note: one, written as the Roman numeral I, comes first

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the verb surrounds the next piece

parts.note: met means encountered
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Momentum came first, met by an American lacking power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: MET goes round P, making MPET. 'by' only places the pieces next to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force or drive that keeps something moving, the same idea as momentum.

clue.text: Flock if it's this

parts.note: a flock is a herd only when spoken, since the word for perceived by ear says the same thing

explanation.definitionFit: Perceived through the ears, which is how a word for a flock of cattle would reach a listener.

clue.text: OK to put on the table of the Queen in the story

definitions.text: OK to put on the table

indicators.note: the Queen's letters are placed inside the word for a story

parts.note: a fable is a story
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A tale about the Queen proves fit to share at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fit to be proposed or presented is suitable to be tabled as an offer.

clue.text: False friend with prince in the 17

indicators.note: a false friend is not genuine, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: and means together with

explanation.surface: A treacherous friend sides with a prince in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False' turns FRIEND into FERDIN. Ferdinand, son of the King of Naples, falls for Miranda in The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand is the King of Naples' son who woos Miranda in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Push needed to get university job?

definitions.text: Push needed to get university job?

parts.words: Push needed to get university job?
parts.note: reads like ambition for a professorship at a university in the city of Bath, but describes a wheeled seat that has to be pushed

explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned wheeled seat for invalids, named after the spa city, is moved by someone pushing it.

clue.text: Try to hold directions in a storm

indicators.note: the first word grips the next piece inside it

parts.note: to tempt is to try, as in tempting fate
E and S are the compass directions east and south

explanation.surface: Trying to hold course in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the verb tempt, as in tempting fate; 'in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, and the word is also the title of Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Part of US state that had prohibition in the 17

indicators.note: only the first part of the state's name is kept

parts.note: California is a US state
a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: A region of an American state that banned alcohol features in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' keeps CALI from CALIFORNIA; 'that had' is a link. Caliban is Prospero's monstrous servant in The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Caliban is the island's native, enslaved by Prospero, in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Heavenly sound in the 17

indicators.note: the word signals that a word is to be said aloud

parts.note: aerial means of the air or sky, so heavenly

explanation.surface: A heavenly noise rings out during the play.
explanation.walkthrough: Ariel is the airy spirit who serves Prospero in The Tempest, so the heavenly reading suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the spirit of the air who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Area for old London criminals or dogs — as a tail unfolds

definitions.text: Area for old London criminals or dogs

indicators.note: the letters open out into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A place for old crooks or hounds appears as a tail uncurls.
explanation.walkthrough: Alsatia was the slang name for Whitefriars in London, a sanctuary for debtors and criminals; Alsatians are also the dogs known elsewhere as German shepherds.
explanation.definitionFit: The cant name for a London district that sheltered wrongdoers, and the region giving Alsatian dogs their name.

clue.text: Green type takes turn in revolutionary engine

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the next piece inside them
turning things upside down, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: a U-turn, so U stands for turn

explanation.surface: An inexperienced sort turns round inside a rotating engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' makes INGENE from ENGINE, and 'takes' puts U before its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: An innocent, naive young woman, especially as a stage role, is an inexperienced or green type.

clue.text: City father's promulgation (part American)

indicators.note: only a part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A city's founder issues a decree, partly American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' keeps only a portion, ROMUL, of promulgation, dropping its first letter and its ending GATION; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Romulus is the legendary founder of Rome, so its father in the civic sense.

clue.text: Pose for king, first getting spruce

parts.note: to sit is to pose for a portrait
K is the abbreviation for king in chess
A is first, as in A1 or the top grade

explanation.surface: Sitting for a king, the first to get tidied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spruce' looks like a verb meaning tidy; it is the tree. 'for' and 'getting' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sitka is a species of spruce tree from Alaska, widely planted for timber.

clue.text: Visible requirement for psychotherapist

definitions.meaning: able to be seen, as when land comes into view
a therapist needs understanding into a patient's mind

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means within view; as one word it means perceptive understanding, which therapy depends on.

clue.text: Fizzy stuff to place round plant

indicators.note: the first word goes around the next piece

parts.note: to set something is to place it
a herb is a plant

explanation.surface: Fizzy stuff to put around a plant, like a fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain sherbet is a fizzy sweet powder, not the frozen dessert Americans know by the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet in Britain is a fizzy powdered sweet, so effervescent stuff.

clue.text: Merchant becoming baddie in the 17

definitions.meaning: the title character of The Merchant of Venice bears this name
Prospero's usurping brother is the villain of The Tempest

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare used the same name for the Venetian merchant and for Prospero's scheming brother.

clue.text: Flag for speed — that's how it usually goes

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Raising a flag for speed is the usual way things go.
explanation.definitionFit: The normal level applying in ordinary cases, as with tax, is the usual going rate.
